data.assessment: In this quiet period the service is already good: 85.0 of 87.4 orders were on time (rate 0.97), with 2.4 late, 0.0 unfinished, p95_wait_s 103 and max_wait_s 351. Most violations are hold_limit overstays (deadline:release 22.0) plus 7.4 blocking_guard evictions. They fall mostly on C, which waits on the road (29.0 waits) and pays 21.2 penalty points, leaving its utility at 9.6 against about 26–27 for A and B. A is the company most blocked by parked robots (647 s) and has the lowest on-time rate (0.94), so the remaining on-time headroom lies mainly in A's blocking and in C's road parking.

proposals.title: Shorten hold_limit from 50s to 40s to reduce blocking of A in the quiet period
proposals.rationale: A is blocked for 647 s of the 1078 s town total and has the most late deliveries (1.6). Forcing parked robots to leave node 8 sooner should cut blocked_s and may convert a few of A's late deliveries into on-time ones. The town-wide gain is capped at about 2.4 orders, so it may not clear min_improvement 1.0, and the gate will decide. Overstay violations, and with them C's penalties, will probably rise, so I expect A yes, B uncertain and C no. This is not the 60s value rejected in D5: it moves the other way, toward less road parking.
proposals.cadl:
# =====================================================================
# robot_town.cadl ─── ロボットの街：3 社の配送ロボットが道路を共有する
#
# 道路網はラズパイマウスのシミュレータと同じ 11 ノード・17 エッジ。
# 3 社（A / B / C）が 2 台ずつロボットを走らせ、ノードは 1 台ずつしか
# 使えない。仕事のないロボットは車庫に戻るか、道路上（中央の交差点 8）
# に止まって次の注文を待つ。止まったロボットは他社の通行をふさぐ。
#
# `# @amend:<名前>` が付いた行は、改正してよいパラメータ。どの層（規則・
# 契約）に属し、どこまで動かしてよいかは constitution.yaml が決める。
# 委員会（COUNCIL）が自分で改正できるのは規則の層だけで、契約の層を
# 変えるには人間の判断が要る。
# =====================================================================

sos:
  name: "RobotTown"
  type: Collaborative             # 独立した 3 社が共通の規則を決める
  version: "1.0.0"

  context:
    environment:
      num_robots:   6
      num_companies: 3
      time_step_ms: 1000

  actors:
    - id: TOWN_STEWARD
      role: "road_steward"
      autonomy: low
      capabilities: [assign_order, record_violation, evict]
      interface:
        input:  [order_request, position_report, node_released, rule_update]
        output: [order_assignment, eviction_notice, regime_notice, violation_report]

    - id: "ROBOT[1..N]"
      role: "delivery_robot"
      autonomy: high
      capabilities: [move, park, pickup, dropoff]
      interface:
        input:  [order_assignment, eviction_notice, regime_notice, amendment_proposal]
        output: [position_report, node_released, ballot]

    - id: COUNCIL
      role: "rule_amendment_body"
      autonomy: medium
      capabilities: [propose_amendment, tally_ballots]
      interface:
        input:  [violation_report, ballot]
        output: [amendment_proposal, rule_update]

  contracts:
    # ── 顧客への約束：注文 1 件ごとのインスタンス（契約の層。人間が決める） ──
    - id: DELIVERY_SLA
      parties: [TOWN_STEWARD, "ROBOT[*]"]
      guarantee:
        - "pickup_time <= 120s"         # @amend:pickup_deadline
        - "dropoff_time <= 120s"        # @amend:dropoff_deadline
      lifecycle:
        states: [Assigned, PickedUp, Delivered, Late]
        initial: Assigned
        terminal: [Delivered, Late]
        transitions:
          - id: pickup
            from: Assigned
            to:   PickedUp
            on:   "ROBOT[i].status == PickedUp"
            deadline: 120s            # @amend:pickup_deadline
            on_violation: { transition: Late, severity: Major }
          - id: dropoff
            from: PickedUp
            to:   Delivered
            on:   "ROBOT[i].status == Delivered"
            deadline: 120s            # @amend:dropoff_deadline
            on_violation: { transition: Late, severity: Major }

    # ── 道路の使い方：道路上に止まるたびに 1 インスタンス ──
    - id: ROAD_USE
      parties: [TOWN_STEWARD, "ROBOT[*]", COUNCIL]
      guarantee:
        - "hold_time <= hold_limit"
      authority:
        decision_holder: COUNCIL
        beta: 0.5
        mode: "collective"
      information:
        alpha: 1.0                    # 規則と違反記録は全社に公開
      incentives:
        type: sanction
        lambda: 0.5                   # @amend:sanction_lambda
        rules:
          - "penalty(ROBOT[i], lambda) when overstay"
      lifecycle:
        states: [Holding, Overstay, Released, Evicted]
        initial: Holding
        terminal: [Released, Evicted]
        transitions:
          - id: release
            from: [Holding, Overstay]
            to:   Released
            on:   "ROBOT[i] -> TOWN_STEWARD : node_released"
            deadline: 40s             # @amend:hold_limit
            on_violation: { transition: Overstay, severity: Minor }
      monitors:
        - id: blocking_guard
          observe: "ROBOT[i].blocking"
          sampling: periodic(1000ms)
          rule: "ROBOT.blocking >= 2 AND state IN [Holding, Overstay]"  # @amend:block_k
          on_match: { transition: Evicted, severity: Major }

  # ── 運用モード：分散（各社が道路上で待つ）⇄ 集中（管理者が待避所を割り当てる） ──
  # 条件は 5 分ごとに、直前 5 分の観測で判定する。
  #   orders_in_window : 3 社の注文の合計件数
  #   blocked_pct      : ロボットが止まっているロボットにふさがれていた時間の割合（%）
  # 集中管理は交差点をふさがれない反面、エッジを 1 台ずつ割り当てるので、
  # 注文が非常に多いと許可待ちが積み重なる。そのときだけ分散に戻す。
  transitions:
    - from: DISTRIBUTED
      to: CENTRALIZED
      condition: "orders_in_window < 22"      # @amend:to_central
      protocol: SWITCH
      safety_invariant: "robots_on_road == 0"
    - from: CENTRALIZED
      to: DISTRIBUTED
      condition: "orders_in_window >= 26"     # @amend:to_distributed
      protocol: SWITCH

  protocols:
    - id: SWITCH
      trigger: "regime_condition_holds"
      steps:
        - "TOWN_STEWARD -> ROBOT[*] : regime_notice"
        - "ROBOT[*] -> TOWN_STEWARD : node_released"
        - "TOWN_STEWARD : activate_regime"
    - id: AMEND
      trigger: "period_end"
      steps:
        - "TOWN_STEWARD -> COUNCIL : violation_report"
        - "COUNCIL -> ROBOT[*] : amendment_proposal"
        - "ROBOT[*] -> COUNCIL : ballot"
        - "COUNCIL : tally_ballots"
        - "COUNCIL -> TOWN_STEWARD : rule_update"

  metrics:
    - id: on_time_deliveries
      formula: "count(Delivered)"
      target: ">= 0.9 * count(orders)"
    - id: blocked_time
      formula: "sum(blocked_robot_seconds)"
      target: "<= 600s"
assumptions: The release violations (22.0) and A's blocked time come mainly from robots parked at node 8 for close to the full hold_limit.
Robots ordered off the road sooner will return to the depot or reposition without creating new congestion in a quiet period.
unknowns: Whether a 40s limit makes C's robots respond to orders more slowly, which would offset A's gain.
How much C's penalty and road_violations rise per seed.

predictions.subject: metric:on_time_deliveries
predictions.note: Small gain, likely at most about 1–2 orders; it may not clear the 1.0 gate.

predictions.subject: metric:road_violations
predictions.note: More holds will exceed the shorter deadline.

predictions.subject: metric:max_wait_s
predictions.note: Less blocking should shorten the worst waits.

predictions.subject: vote:A
predictions.note: A is the most blocked company and pays no penalties.

predictions.subject: vote:C
predictions.note: C parks most and would collect more overstay penalties.

proposals.title: Set sanction_lambda from 0.5 to 0.0 in the quiet period as a measured mitigation for C
proposals.rationale: C pays 21.2 penalty points, which brings its utility down to 9.6 against about 26–27 for A and B. This is the outstanding mitigation promised in D1–D5. D3 rejected removing the sanction in a busy period because on-time fell by 3.0 and road violations rose sharply. What has changed is the season: in this quiet period (arrivals every 120 s) congestion is light, so the behavioural cost may be small. The objective gate (+1.0 on-time) and the same-seed customer metrics will show whether it harms customers. If it passes, all three companies would likely vote yes, since every company's penalties disappear.

proposals.why_human: The human rejected removing the sanction in D3 (busy period) because it cost customers and raised road violations. This re-proposal rests on a changed context (quiet demand), so the human should decide whether a season-dependent sanction is acceptable at all. That decision should use the same-seed changes in on_time_deliveries, p95_wait_s, max_wait_s and road_violations. If it is adopted, a busy-season revert would also be needed.
assumptions: In a quiet period, removing the penalty changes parking behaviour less than it did in the busy period measured in D3.
Utility for all companies rises mechanically once penalties are zero, so all three vote yes unless on-time falls.
unknowns: Whether road_violations and blocked_s rise enough to hurt A's on-time deliveries.
Whether the on-time gain reaches the 1.0 gate; it may be neutral or negative, as in D3.

predictions.subject: metric:sanction_total
predictions.note: A lambda of 0 removes all penalty points.

predictions.subject: metric:road_violations
predictions.note: Without penalties, robots may park longer.

predictions.subject: metric:on_time_deliveries
predictions.note: Unlikely to clear the +1.0 gate, but this measures the customer cost of the mitigation for C.

predictions.subject: vote:C
predictions.note: C gains most from removing penalties.

predictions.subject: vote:A
predictions.note: A pays no penalties now; it votes yes unless its on-time count falls.
